prompt: I am trying to understand why some k6 scripts behave fine in init but then start failing once the test is actually running with a lot of VUs, especially when code tries to load modules dynamically instead of only at startup. When the runtime is under pressure, does k6 intentionally “freeze” module resolution after initialization, and if so what exactly counts as already resolved versus a new module that should be rejected? I am particularly curious about what happens with relative specifiers that depend on which module is currently executing, since that seems like it could get confusing when the call stack comes from different places. Can you show, with real runs, whether a module that was imported during init can still be required later by VUs, while a never-seen module reliably fails, and what the exact error or warning looks like in each case? Temporary scripts may be used for observation, but the repository itself should remain unchanged and anything temporary should be cleaned up afterward.
